🐛 Describe the bug
Context
FX Graph Mode Quantization is an automated flow for quantization (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/quantization.html#prototype-fx-graph-mode-quantization), since we may target different backends that supports quantization, and different backends have different support for quantized ops/dtypes etc. we developed BackendConfig that is used to configure quantization flow for various backends. More details in https://github.com/pytorch/rfcs/blob/master/RFC-0019-Extending-PyTorch-Quantization-to-Custom-Backends.md
The main goal for this task is to make some parts of hardcoded things configurable.
Task
For a function call like: F.conv2d(input, weight, bias, ...), we need to identify which argument is weight, bias or input, right now we have two hardcoded dictionaries that's used to identify the weight and bias for different operators: WEIGHT_INDEX_DICT (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/utils.py#L57) and BIAS_INDEX_DICT (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/utils.py#L69). most of the other configurations are defined in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/backend_config/native.py#L243
We should use BackendConfig to define these configurations as well, in this case, we can use https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/backend_config/backend_config.py#L305 (_set_input_type_to_index) to define the map from "weight"/"bias" to the index of the argument in the operator. e.g.
F.linear(input, weight, bias), then {"input": 0, "weight": 1, "bias": 2}, example: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/backend_config/tensorrt.py#L33, we can move these configurations to the operator configurations in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/backend_config/_common_operator_config_utils.py#L200,
e.g.
# this in a configuration for F.conv1d
conv_configs.append(
            BackendPatternConfig(convs.func)
                .set_observation_type(observation_type)  # noqa: E131
                .set_dtype_configs(dtype_configs))
                . _set_input_type_to_index({"weight": 1, "bias": 2})
# and do this for all the operators in WEIGHT_INDEX_DICT and BIAS_INDEX_DICT

in the end we should be able to remove the use of WEIGHT_INDEX_DICT and BIAS_INDEX_DICT in https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/ao/quantization/fx/prepare.py, and derive these two dictionaries from configurations.
Versions
master
cc @jerryzh168 @jianyuh @raghuramank100 @jamesr66a @vkuzo @ezyang @SherlockNoMad

TL;DR: summon_full_params(offload_to_cpu=True) does not free the GPU copy of the unsharded flattened parameter, so both a CPU and GPU copy exist when in the context.

Repro:
def test_cpu_offload_full_param_padded(self):
    model = nn.Linear(5, 5).cuda()
    fsdp_model = FSDP(model)
    with FSDP.summon_full_params(fsdp_model, offload_to_cpu=True):
        ...

(1) Add a print() like
print(f"[Rank {self.rank}] _full_param_padded: {p._full_param_padded.device} {p._full_param_padded.storage().size()}")

after this line:

  
    
      pytorch/torch/distributed/fsdp/fully_sharded_data_parallel.py
    
    
         Line 2563
      in
      6c60a65
    
  
  
    

        
          
           full_param = full_param.to(torch.device("cpu")) 
        
    
  


(2) Add a print() like
print(f"[Rank {self.rank}] _full_param_padded: {p._full_param_padded.device} {p._full_param_padded.storage().size()}")

before this line:

  
    
      pytorch/torch/distributed/fsdp/fully_sharded_data_parallel.py
    
    
         Line 2594
      in
      6c60a65
    
  
  
    

        
          
           full_param = full_param.to(self.compute_device) 
        
    
  


We see a print like:
[Rank 0] _full_param_padded: cuda:0 30
[Rank 0] _full_param_padded: cuda:0 30
[Rank 1] _full_param_padded: cuda:1 30
[Rank 1] _full_param_padded: cuda:1 30


I think that the move to CPU should be done in-place to allow the GPU copy of the (padded) unsharded flattened parameter to be freed. Otherwise, full model state dict may unexpectedly hit an OOM with offload_to_cpu=True. (Full model state dict will recurse down the module tree, so at the leaf module, all parent modules' parameters are unsharded, representing the peak memory usage. For large models, this cannot fit in GPU, so offload_to_cpu=True is necessary.)
Like the other summon_full_params() issue, I am addressing this in my refactoring, so if this is not blocking, there is no need to land an intermediate fix.

If parameter mixed precision is enabled, the root FSDP instance does not summon_full_params() in full precision as expected if summon_full_params() is called after the forward (but before the backward).
The reason is that for the root FSDP, we have self.reshard_after_forward = False, so the unsharded flattened parameter is kept in memory after the forward. As a result, _rebuild_full_params() takes the no-op code path and does not force a full precision all-gather:
  
    
      pytorch/torch/distributed/fsdp/fully_sharded_data_parallel.py
    
    
        Lines 3291 to 3294
      in

               p._full_param_padded.storage().size()  # type: ignore[attr-defined] 
        

        
          
               == p._full_param_padded.size().numel()  # type: ignore[attr-defined] 
        

        
          
           ):

Right a limiting factor for TorchInductor on smaller models is fixed launched overheads of Triton kernels.  We are relying on cudagraphs to save us here, but that will not work for dynamic shapes.

Triton currently only supports CUDA Capability >= 7.0
Today, I tried the Inductor unit tests (and eventually Triton unit tests) on a Titan X Maxwell GPU (CC 5.2).
Things pretty much universally failed with Internal Triton PTX codegen error related to using atomic ops and other ops related to CC 6.0+ or CC 7.0+
Inductor should do runtime checks for CC 7.0 and if not true, throw a warning and fallback to Eager.
We have similar kind of checks in PyTorch runtime (for much older GPUs though): https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/master/torch/cuda/__init__.py#L143-L150

Currently, guards in TorchInductor are only partially implemented.  Up until now we have relied on static shape guards at the dynamo level to protect both AOT Autograd and Inductor.  In the future we should:

Enable torchdynamo.config.dynamic_shapes=True
Possibly add a caching layer (or reuse the dynamo code cache)
Pipe symbolic shapes through AOT Autograd (dispatcher symbolic shapes is a blocker for this)
Pass accumulated guards in TorchInductor (and AOT Autograd) up to the guarding/caching layer above

TorchInductor has two types of guards:
https://github.com/pytorch/torchdynamo/blob/a4e39a480094a5d25fefba69e6895bd5c694d07e/torchinductor/sizevars.py#L16
https://github.com/pytorch/torchdynamo/blob/a4e39a480094a5d25fefba69e6895bd5c694d07e/torchinductor/sizevars.py#L26
Which are generated and stored in a list here:
https://github.com/pytorch/torchdynamo/blob/a4e39a480094a5d25fefba69e6895bd5c694d07e/torchinductor/sizevars.py#L41
We should add some code to filter guards (some guards might trivially imply other guards).  We can use sympy subs/solve for this.  Also Z3 would be candidate for more complex removal.
The code to map the list of guards to a generated "check" function is not yet implemented.

📚 The doc issue

device - the device of the constructed tensor. If None and data is a tensor then the device of data is used. If None and data is not a tensor then the result tensor is constructed on the CPU.

However, if None and data is not a tensor, then the result tensor actually is constructed on the current device for the default tensor type, like torch.empty, torch.zeros and torch.ones.
Suggest a potential alternative/fix
the device of the constructed tensor. Default: If None and data is a tensor, uses the device of data. If None and data is not a tensor, uses the current device for the default tensor type (see torch.set_default_tensor_type()). device will be the CPU for CPU tensor types and the current CUDA device for CUDA tensor types.
